value.body: A pharmacy owner runs a licensed chemist shop that sells medicines to the public. The owner is often the registered pharmacist on the counter, or employs one. A typical day is dispensing, ordering stock from distributors, checking expiry dates, billing and keeping the records that the drug licence requires.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: D.Pharm or B.Pharm + State Pharmacy Council registration

items.label: Licence
items.value: Retail drug licence from the State Drugs Control department
items.note: Under the Drugs and Cosmetics Rules, 1945; a registered pharmacist must be in charge

items.label: Jan Aushadhi Kendras opened
items.note: As on 31 Dec 2025; government target of 25,000 by March 2027

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Register with the State Pharmacy Council and usually gain experience at an existing pharmacy first. Then arrange premises and capital, and apply for retail sale drug licences from the state drug controller. Opening a Jan Aushadhi Kendra under the government scheme is another route.

value.title: At a glance
items: Starting needs money for premises and stock, and income depends on location and footfall.
Chain pharmacies and online pharmacies add competition.
Some owners add services such as home delivery or tie-ups with nearby clinics.

competition.note: D.Pharm graduates in 2023-24 at institutions that reported to AISHE — everyone finishing that degree, not only those entering this role.
competition.source: AISHE 2023-24, Table 34 (programme-wise out-turn), Ministry of Education

women.note: Share of women among D.Pharm graduates in 2023-24 — the entry degree, not people already working in this role.
women.source: AISHE 2023-24, Table 34 (programme-wise out-turn), Ministry of Education
